statement.text:
Let form(G) be the formation generated by a finite group G. Suppose that G
has a unique composition series 1 ◁ G1 ◁ G2 ◁ G and the consecutive factors of this
series are Zp , X, Zq , where p and q are primes and X is a non-abelian simple group.
Is it true that form(G) has infinitely many subformations if and only if p = q?
                                                                            V. P. Burichenko
